english.title: Knowingly / recklessly give a regulator false / misleading information
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), in purported compliance with a requirement imposed by or under the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, namely **(..SPECIFY THE REQUIREMENT..), knowingly or recklessly gave the

(A)_[Financial Conduct]_
(B)_[Prudential Regulation]_

Authority information which was false or misleading in a material particular, namely **(..SPECIFY THE INFORMATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 398(1) and (3) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.

english.notes:
(i) Section 398(1) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 applies only to a requirement in relation to which no other provision of this Act creates an offence in connection with the giving of information.
(ii) Section 401 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that proceedings for offences may be instituted in England and Wales only by the 'appropriate regulator' (either the Financial Conduct or the Prudential Regulation Authority) or the Secretary of State or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.(iii) From 31st December 2024, Regulation 24(3) of the Data Reporting Services Regulations 2024 (SI 2024/107) applies section 398 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 for the purposes of the Regulations and makes it an offence for any person who, in purported compliance with any requirement imposed by or under the Data Reporting Services Regulations 2024 within the meaning of regulation 2(4), to knowingly or recklessly give information which is false or misleading in a material particular to the FCA or another person, knowing they would provide it to, or use it for the purpose of providing information to, the FCA. This offence as applied by the Data Reporting Service Regulations 2024 is not currently on PNLD. If this is of interest, please contact PNLD.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
